text: Two bolted sentries. The far one has the good lenses. I ordered one set. It seemed enough at the time.
You will notice that nothing in front of the near one takes a portal. I noticed first. That is why.
It will never see itself. That does not mean nobody has an opinion of it.
One of them shot the other, and then itself. I have seen committees end the same way.
That is the lens fitter's room. He fitted one set of lenses and asked for a day off. I am still considering it.
This crate has a lens in one face. Light that goes into the crate comes out of the lens. Somebody patented that. I have their badge somewhere.
At present it is lighting a wall. The wall is not grateful. The receivers might be.
The crate cannot be in two places. I have checked. The light, on the other hand, has never been particular about where it comes from.
One beam, three receivers, and a crate that did the thinking. I have put it forward for your job.

The door wants light on the receiver and a sentry on the plate. Both sentries are bolted down. The laser is behind you. I have had it turned up. It does not care who is in the way. I have always admired that about it.
A bolt holds a sentry for exactly as long as the sentry is worth bolting down. I will say no more. I have already been told off for saying that.
You burned out two sentries with a laser I installed to open doors, and then you weighed the door down with one of them. The list of things you have repurposed is getting longer.
They watch the door. They watch each other's backs. In all the years they have stood there, neither has once looked up. I find that very relatable.
Two of them are only standing there out of habit. The third I bolted down myself, and it has never thanked me. Bolts do nothing about what arrives from above.
You have found the maintenance bunk. Maintenance never did. I stopped sending the reminders some years ago.
That is a spark. It travels in a straight line, bounces off whatever it meets, and gives up after a while. I have worked with people like that.
The socket would like it. The socket is past the field, behind a shutter, at the end of a flue. I did not want it to be easy for the spark either.
The field takes your portals away. It has never once taken anything from the spark. Think about which of you is better off.
The socket has its spark, and you still have your eyebrows. I had a small bet with myself. I have lost it.
The door is on a camera scale. It wants two. Over there, past the acid. The launch pad will take anything you give it.
Count the cameras in this room. Now count the ones the door wants. I did the sum before you came in. It is why I am not worried about my cameras. I should be.
